text: This is the single most common block of code you'll write in ServiceNow server-side scripting. Four lines, four distinct jobs, and today we're breaking down exactly what each one does.

First, new GlideRecord of incident creates the cursor, nothing fetched yet. Then addQuery active true, and addQuery priority 1, each add one filter condition — and by default, multiple addQuery calls on the same GlideRecord combine with AND, not OR, so this finds incidents that are active and priority 1, both required. Then query actually sends those conditions to the database — nothing before that line touches the database at all, addQuery only builds things up in memory. And finally, while gr dot next walks through the results one row at a time.

Next does two things in one call: it advances the cursor to the next matching row, and it returns true if there was a row to move to, or false once the results run out. That's the entire reason the while loop shape exists — it's the only correct way to drain a result set, because next is simultaneously the move-forward operation and the are-we-done check.

There are two real ways to read a field, and both show up constantly in production code. getValue of a field name always returns a plain JavaScript string. Dot notation, like gr dot short underscore description, returns a GlideElement object instead — but a GlideElement automatically stringifies to its display value whenever it's used in a string context, so both lines here log the exact same text.

Worth repeating because it trips people up: addQuery active true, addQuery assigned_to current user, addQuery priority 1 — that's active AND assigned to me AND priority 1. All three conditions must be true for a row to match. If you actually need OR logic between conditions, that's a different method entirely, and it's coming in Lesson 15.

Create, filter, execute, loop — that's the canonical GlideRecord query. Next lesson, we go the other direction: inserting new records, updating existing ones, and deleting them, with setValue, insert, update, and deleteRecord.
